findings.suggested_investigation: In the k2.saveevents library source (outside this packet), check whether a detour on 0x008529E0 (LoadAutosaveSlot) fires K2SE_LOAD_REQUEST with folder "000001 - AUTOSAVE". If it does not, confirm by reading the library's hook list. The contract test common_contract_test.cpp:897-925 covers only the event mask and callback, not this path.
findings.why_it_matters: The old LoadAutosaveSlot detour was the only hook on the PCAUTOSAVE load path, which bypasses LoadGame. If k2.saveevents only emits LOAD_REQUEST from LoadGame, loading a module autosave entry no longer restores that save's hotbar profile, so the bar keeps the previous session's live profile. This is a silent regression in a normal play path.

findings.why_it_matters: Previously the HUD detours were installed directly by KPM and did not depend on another mod. Now, if hud-host is absent or fails to connect, the bar and its controls silently stop rendering or updating. The only signal is a log line. This is a behaviour change when that dependency is missing.

findings.evidence: if (!p && characterKey == "objfffffffd") { p = find("player"); if (!p) p = find("exile"); }  HotbarLogic.h:85 maps both "player" and "exile" to the same canonical key "objfffffffd".
findings.suggested_investigation: Check how profiles named "Player" versus "Exile" are created (the editor and the Parse path in HotbarConfig.h:353-359) and whether both can coexist in one file. Then add a case to config_roundtrip_test.cpp or hotbar_logic_test.cpp covering both profiles present, to confirm which one wins and whether that is intended.
findings.why_it_matters: When a save has both a "Player" and an "Exile" profile, both map to one character. The fallback here only consults the "exile" profile when "player" is absent, so the "Exile" bindings are silently ignored. The fallback also applies only when the exact lowercase key is missing, so a profile written under the other name never gets used.
